One problem people are concerned with are sockpuppets. One way to combat the threat of sockpuppets is to give people an opportunity to prove they are not using multiple accounts. One way to do this is to let people prove their identity to voat admins. Once they have proven their identity, everyone would be able to see that their account has be "verified", but they would not necessarily be able to see the users actual identity (unless the user wanted them to). The benefit, then, is that each person could only create one verified account. (On the other hand, a person can still create multiple unverified accounts).

I think the verification should be done through a trusted third party. (There seem to not be too many third parties that can do this, but it seems the UK government can (for UK citizens), and if you do a google search, you can find newer companies that are trying to be able to do this as well. Presumably this will be more ubiquitous as time goes on, so if this is not feasible now it will be soon.) The reason I think a third party should be used is that the identity verification problem is independent from voat, so there is no reason voat developers should spend their time finding a solution to the problem when many other companies already are.

Verified accounts might be allowed to use voat features that would otherwise be abused by people with multiple accounts. The only drawback is that the third party services would probably cost money, and so giving extra features to verified accounts would give an unfair advantage to people with more money to spend.
Opt-in to verify that you are a real person and not a duplicate or fake account.

I think it's important to give unpopular speech an opportunity to have a voice and people often feel more comfortable doing that when they are anonymous. Otherwise they just go along with the crowd so they don't get socially shunned. I'm not sure what you have in mind with this verification thing but it sounds like it would involve turning anonymous people into second class citizens.

I agree that it would have a negative effect on "unverified" accounts, and that is may be unfair if the third party verifiers charge money for their services, and not everyone wants to pay this money.

But to address your point about anonymity, notice that I am saying the verified user needs only to prove their identity to voat admins, no the voat users. Thus they may still choose to remain anonymous to other voat users.

In fact, I believe it is possible to do even better. It should be possible (but probably tricky) for a third party company to create a unique hash from each identity (for example, the somehow hash the name, place of birth, birthday, etc). The third party verifier can then reveal this has to voat without revealing the users actual identity. Then as long as voat make sure no two accounts have the same hash, they can ensure there are no duplicate accounts without even knowing any user's identity.
This removes anonymity without actually guaranteeing that the user's account is unique.
